text:
Dmitri Simashev had one point in 28 NHL games last season. This season the 21-year-old has four goals, all of them in his last ten games, including a high-slot wrist shot past Carter Hart that Jesse Granger of The Athletic noted came a shift after he fanned on a one-timer. Utah's video team even featured him joining an odd-man rush. For a defenseman known for his skating and his defense, that's a new wrinkle.

The hot stretch is earned: his own chances over those ten games are worth 1.2 expected goals against 0.8 usually, and his ice time is up more than two minutes a night. Four goals on 2.1 expected for the season still means some of it will cool. Our talent range has him around 8 goals.

The work in progress is the defense. Utah takes 48% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, almost 12 points worse than without him. The sixth overall pick in 2023, taken one spot before Matvei Michkov, sits about where history says he should: 25 of the 27 defensemen picked 4th to 8th since 2005 with four-plus seasons reached 200 games, and their median first full season was 0.30 points a game. He's at 0.29.
